clue.text: Always in favour of safeguards

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
keeps as a verb: protects or safeguards

explanation.surface: Someone who always supports protective measures.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'for keeps' means permanently, for good, which is the adverb always.

clue.text: Tending to fall over kid's misplaced computer accessory

parts.note: floppy means limp, inclined to flop

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A clumsy child has lost a piece of computer kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy disk was a removable magnetic storage medium used with older computers.

clue.text: Contemplating turning back

definitions.note: read as a gerund, the act of contemplating, which is a noun like the answer
definitions.meaning: first meaning: serious thought or meditation
second meaning: the throwing back of light or sound from a surface

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone considering a retreat; the two parts are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflection is both careful thought and the physical bouncing back of light from a mirror or surface.

clue.text: Listlessness regularly seen in Turin

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Boredom is a common sight in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for weary boredom and lack of interest.

clue.text: Really quite attractive, in a sugary way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, while the answer is an adjective meaning prettified to excess

parts.note: pretty as an adverb means fairly or quite, as in 'pretty good'
pretty as an adjective means good-looking

explanation.surface: A description of something charming but overly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty-pretty describes something affectedly or excessively pretty, cloyingly cute rather than truly beautiful.

clue.text: Train some dolphins

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to educate or drill
second meaning: the collective noun for a group of dolphins or fish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests teaching dolphins tricks; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is a verb for instructing, and a school is the collective name for a pod-like group of sea creatures.

clue.text: Blushed and wept about male child

indicators.note: the word for crying goes around the others, surrounding them

parts.note: to cry is to weep
M is the abbreviation for male
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A parent went red and cried over their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male child' looks like one unit giving a single word, but it splits into an abbreviation and a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimson, as a verb, is to turn deep red, so crimsoned means went red in the face.

clue.text: Partner caught by coarse fellow making pig noise

indicators.note: something caught is held inside its captor, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an oik is British slang for a crude, uncouth person
in bridge, North partners South, so N can stand for partner

explanation.surface: A boorish man grabs his partner and grunts like a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge convention: the four players are N, S, E and W, and N and S are partners, as are E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the imitative word for the grunting sound a pig makes.

clue.text: Student's beginning to understand party game

parts.note: L for learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A student starts to get the hang of a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party game' reads as one phrase, but the party is a wordplay piece and only 'game' defines. Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple children's board game in which counters race round a board by dice throws.

clue.text: Crimes of those who receive stolen goods

parts.note: taken as written
a fence is slang for a dealer in stolen property

explanation.surface: A description of the crimes committed by handlers of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but 'of' is a piece in its own right, joined to the slang word for receivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are breaches of the law, a straightforward synonym for crimes.

clue.text: Reactionary man behaved badly

indicators.note: a reactionary wants to go backwards, so the name is read from end to start

parts.note: a man's name

explanation.surface: A right-wing man misbehaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' here stands for a particular man's first name, a convention in which any name may be clued this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to do wrong, so having sinned is having behaved badly in a moral sense.

clue.text: Cost to the NHS of medical certificate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken whimsically: the invoice the health service pays
second meaning: a document declaring someone free of disease

explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; the first half reads the phrase literally as a bill sent to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of health was a certificate confirming a ship or person carried no infection, as in 'a clean bill of health'.

clue.text: I practised a complicated branch of medicine

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A doctor recalls having worked in a difficult medical specialty.
explanation.definitionFit: Paediatrics is the medical specialty dealing with children and their illnesses.

clue.text: Batsman needs this, after batting in Leeds and getting a duck, then 49

indicators.note: batting about suggests knocking things around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
IL is 49 in Roman numerals, one less than fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats at Leeds, is out for nought, then makes 49.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket gives the scene: willow bats are treated with an oil to keep them supple, and Headingley in Leeds is a Test ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers rub this flax-seed oil into new willow bats to protect the wood, so a batsman needs it.

clue.text: Prisoner has to live without right to review

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
a con is a convict
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An inmate must live without his rights, pending a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without right' looks like 'lacking right', but 'without' means outside and the right is then added on.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider a decision is to review it, thinking it over again.

clue.text: Do the same thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'do.' is the written abbreviation used in lists
second meaning: the word said to mean 'likewise, as before'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an instruction to copy someone; 'Do' is actually the abbreviation, so both halves name the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto marks or the abbreviation 'do.' signal a repetition of what is written above, i.e. the same again.

clue.text: Forgets about appearance

parts.note: over means about, as in 'arguing over money'
one's looks are one's appearance

explanation.surface: Someone forgets how they look.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to miss or neglect it, much as to forget it.

clue.text: I soon leap about and dance!

indicators.note: leaping about suggests moving around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An eager dancer announces they will soon be jumping around the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The polonaise is a stately Polish processional dance, also a musical form used by Chopin.

clue.text: Unfortunately one's fated to be unable to hear at all

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is things going awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the fodder, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A sad observation that someone is doomed to total deafness.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-deaf is the idiom for completely deaf, without any hearing whatsoever.

clue.text: Nightclub in Sheffield is cold

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: runs from the last letter of the city through to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A complaint that a Sheffield club is chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Sheffield' reads as the club's location, but 'in' tells you to look inside the words themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or venue where people dance to recorded music at night.

clue.text: Way of printing missive to papers

parts.note: a missive is a letter
the press means the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to print a letter sent to the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Letterpress is a method of printing from raised inked type pressed onto paper.

clue.text: Perhaps Fife's favourite musical instrument?

parts.note: surface reading: the instrument best loved by the people of Fife, the Scottish county
setter's reading: a fife is itself a small flute, so its 'favourite' would be its own wind family, and Scotland suggests the bag variety too

explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a region of Scotland, land of bagpipes; a fife is also a small flute, so its 'favourite' instruments are its own kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipes are wind instruments, especially bagpipes, which a Scottish county or a small flute would naturally favour.

clue.text: In the middle of Birmingham I danced around!

indicators.note: the letters are lying around inside the run of words, not taken from a single word

parts.note: lies across the end of the city, the pronoun and the start of the verb

explanation.surface: Someone recalls dancing joyfully in central Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the middle of' looks like the instruction to take central letters; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning surrounded by, in the middle of something.

clue.text: I came across retired couple

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Someone bumped into a pair of pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for a romantic couple, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: Measure oxygen contained in shooting star

indicators.note: says one element is held inside the other, placed within its letters

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Instructions to gauge the oxygen held in a falling star.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol goes between the last two letters of the measuring device.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is the streak of light from space debris burning up, popularly called a shooting star.

clue.text: Scrap with American chap about way onto motorway

parts.note: a slip is a small scrap, as of paper

indicators.note: the man's name goes around the other letter, encircling it

parts.note: a man's name
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A fight with a US man near a motorway entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a small piece. A slip road is the British term for an on-ramp or off-ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short road by which traffic joins or leaves a motorway, an on-ramp.

clue.text: Mother's request for material

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; the 's is just possessive joining it on
an ask is a request

explanation.surface: A mother asking for some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, originally silk, named after Damascus.

clue.text: Painter and musician

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American artist James McNeill ...
second meaning: one who whistles tunes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests two people; they are two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler was a famous 19th-century painter, and anyone who whistles a tune is a kind of musician.
